english:
First of all, I thank Mother and Jesus for allowing me to stand through this situation with Neenu today.
My name is Jitto. We come from Mundakkayam in Kottayam district. Last June 27th, my wife was eight months pregnant. At that time,
due to a complication, on June 27th we went to Mundakkayam Medical Trust Hospital.
By then, my wife had developed jaundice and her liver condition had deteriorated severely.
Her condition became very critical, and then we were advised to take my wife to Kottayam Carithas Hospital as soon as possible.
We went to Kottayam Hospital and had the baby delivered via C-section as quickly as possible.
By then, my wife’s condition had become very serious.
She was put on a ventilator, and after two days of treatment there, her condition worsened further.
Then we took her to Aster Medcity Hospital in Ernakulam.
There, she continued to remain on the ventilator.
The doctors said there was no other way except a liver transplant. For that, Neenu’s father’s younger brother’s son
came forward, ready to donate his liver. However,
by then, the doctors said the condition had worsened and there was little hope for the future.
It was a situation where there was not even a 10% chance of survival.
While I was crying uncontrollably in front of the hospital, Neenu’s elder sisters
showed me a newspaper and shared a similar experience as a testimony.
After showing the testimony, they said, “Look Jitto, our situation is the same.
We were crying here too and nothing happened, so let’s go to Kreupasanam as soon as possible.”
To be honest, I had no great faith at that time. I had come here before,
but I had no real faith here; everything about going to a church felt insignificant. Yet I was in that situation.
Following what my sisters said, we called a taxi and went to Kreupasanam as quickly as possible.
When we arrived and got out. At the hospital, my mother called
and told me that even a small INR amount had decreased as the doctors had mentioned.
I was told, “Did you hear?”
Then, no matter what, I cried uncontrollably there and prayed to Mother, saying I cannot manage without her,
I told everyone there that my wife’s condition was very critical.
Everyone prayed, and I took covenant.
While I was coming down crying, one of the sisters serving here asked me, “Son, why are you crying?” I told her, “This is the situation, sister.”
Then she asked me, “Did you take the covenant?” I said, “Yes, I did.” She replied, “Then why are you crying, son? Be strong and go forward. Mother will take care of the rest.”
But to be honest, at that time I did not have much faith. Anyway, after taking the covenant, I went back to the hospital. That night, together with our sisters,
we all sat, knelt down in front of the ICU, and prayed.
After praying there, since attendants are not usually allowed inside the ICU at night, I asked for permission to go in once.
With permission, I took the covenant oil inside and applied it on Neenu’s forehead. She was lying unconscious, but at that very moment,
she slightly opened and blinked her eyes. Just a small blink.
From then on, every day and every night, we used to light a candle near the place where we stayed in the hospital.
We would light the candle at night and again at 5:30 in the morning, praying continuously.
From that point, little by little, everything started to turn positive.
The doctors began to say that her INR levels were coming down, SGPT levels were reducing—
small signs of improvement started appearing. After two or three days, the doctors said,
“The liver is beginning to show signs of recovery. Let us wait and see.”
Until then, the liver had completely failed. Both the liver and kidneys were in a state of total failure.
But from then on, step by step, things began to improve.
For about 30 days she remained on the ventilator,
and today, we believe it is only through the intercession of Mother Mary and the grace of Jesus that Neenu could be brought to this situation.
It was the covenant oil that I applied on her forehead. After applying that oil, the change began to happen.
Today, it is only by God’s grace that I have received Neenu back in this condition.
I thank Mother Mary and Jesus a thousand times. During this period, when she was in that condition,
I also used to take the Kreupasanam covenant paper and give it to the many people standing and crying outside the ICU in the hospital.
Even though my own heart was broken, I told them, “Don’t worry. Just pray. Mother will take care of it.”
I went to many, gave them the paper, and consoled them.
At the hospital, I was able to comfort and strengthen many people in this way.
I also used to listen to the prayers from Kreupasanam and the covenant prayers while sitting there.
I would listen, and in between, I even started reading the Bible. To tell you the truth, I had never read the Bible before.
But at the hospital, my uncle bought me a Bible. Sitting there, I began reading the Bible and praying.
In this way, by God’s grace, Neenu was brought back to life in this situation.
I thank Mother Mary and Jesus a thousand times. I also thank Kreupasanam Mother very much.
And I thank Jesus abundantly. Neenu is now gradually regaining her awareness, and her memory is also coming back.
She has no memory at all of what happened while I was in the hospital, because everything she knows now is only what others have told her afterwards.
She was lying there for a whole month, but she was not aware of anything. Suddenly, one day, she opened her eyes in the hospital without knowing what had happened.
She did not even remember that she had been pregnant. Everything was forgotten. Now, slowly, all those memories are coming back.
For that reason, I thank Mother Mary a thousand times. Psalm 75:1 says:
“O God, we give thanks to You, we give thanks to You; we call upon Your name and declare Your wonderful deeds.”
This son, Jitto John, together with his wife and children, is giving thanks to Mother Mary and to Jesus for the great blessing received by his family—
the miracle of getting back his wife’s life.
He testifies that his wife was on the ventilator, her liver had failed,
and doctors had said she needed a liver transplant. Her internal organs had stopped functioning.
The chances of survival were so minimal that doctors could not even give assurance that she would return.
It was at that point that his relatives encouraged him to come and pray at the feet of Mother Mary in this holy place.
When he came here, he says, he did not feel any strong faith. He had come here before as well, but nothing great had touched him then.
But now, with his wife’s life slipping away, he entered this church with deep cries from within his heart, pleading that she should not be lost.
And just as he entered, he received a phone call with a positive message:
“There is some movement—her hands and feet are slightly moving, there is some change.”
This is what we always see with the covenant: whenever someone comes here broken and shattered, seeking Mother’s help,
the moment they reach Mother’s presence, she gives a message of hope.
For she says, “I see you. I am with you. I am holding your hand. There will be a decision in this matter.” That is the first signal Mother gives.
That is how this son came into this church. He says, “I came here and wept bitterly before Mother.”
Even when all the negative things people said were ringing in my ears,
I entrusted everything to Mother, asking her to help me.
I then took the covenant, submitted my wife’s photo for Fr. Joseph’s anointing prayer, and prayed with all my heart.
Even as I stood there, I was full of fear because the situation could turn any way.
But we all know—through the anointing service of the Father—thousands of children receive healing, life issues are resolved, and people are restored to health.
We have seen and heard such testimonies again and again.
He says, “After all this, I once again left this place with tears in my eyes.”
On the way, a volunteer asked me, “Son, why are you crying?” I explained the situation, and he comforted me, saying:
“Didn’t you entrust everything to Mother? Now go with courage.”
He let me go with those words of comfort. Every single one of these is Mother’s intervention.
We know that the special grace of the covenant is this communication. That volunteer may have seen 500 or even 1,000 people that day, yet have spoke only to one.
“Son, why are you crying? Be courageous and go forward.” While standing here,
another brother told, “We can pray.” This is all communication—Mother Mary, through her messengers, always intervenes in our lives, sending messages whenever there is a problem.
The brother says, “I went back and began to pray again. From the hospital, every day the news turned positive.
They said, ‘She is improving. The liver has started working. We can move forward. Things will be alright.’
The other internal organs also began to function better. One by one, everything improved.
Today, as this family stands before this altar, they declare: It was Mother’s great protection. From the very moment I entrusted my wife, who was at the point of death, into Mother’s hands through the covenant, until today, Mother carried her.
She gave her to Jesus, and He gave her back life and health.
Today Mother has helped this family to come together to this altar, to glorify the name of her Divine Son, and to witness to her apparition.
This is not a small testimony—it is the testimony of a person who has crossed over from death into life.
Another point the brother mentioned is this: Do we make an effort to lower our status, to humble ourselves? That is the question.
He says, “For me, giving like this was difficult. Doing these things was hard. I had never read the Bible before.
But I reorganized my life. I humbled myself. I began to read the Bible.
I began to pray. I began to give out the Kreupasanam covenant papers to others. Even while I myself was broken,
I shared words of hope with those who were weeping, telling them, ‘Mother will take care of you.’ I handed them the covenant papers.”
This change in attitude is what keeps the covenant burning in our lives—because it turns us into people who switch God “on” in their lives.
Through this change of heart, this family stands at this altar today, with the joy of heaven, thanking Mother.
As we glorify God’s name, let us pray that He may take up our life’s tragedies, resolve them quickly,
and help us to become witnesses of her apparition.
For this new life given to this sister, for the new joy given to this family, and for the renewed faith received by this brother,
let us thank Mother Mary and her Divine Son, clapping our hands, and offer this testimony.
Extraordinary divine experiences can also become yours.
